_readme: Edit the questions here, then run: npm run faq (rewrites the questions and their Google data in faq.html).

questions.q: How do I convert my TU percentage to a US GPA?
questions.a: Enter each course with its credits and mark, and pick the grading scale printed on your transcript. Each course is converted to a US letter grade, then averaged by credits to give a GPA on the 4.0 or 4.3 scale.

questions.q: Which grading scale should I choose for BSc CSIT?
questions.a: Choose the scale that matches the grading table on your transcript. For Tribhuvan University BSc CSIT, the transcript lists First Division as 70% and above, which is the “Tribhuvan University Undergraduate (Pass at 40)” scale.

questions.q: What if a course is out of 200, like the internship?
questions.a: Type the mark as marks/full marks, for example 187/200, and it is converted to a percentage (93.5%). Enter the course’s credit hours as printed on your transcript, such as 6 for the BSc CSIT internship.

questions.q: Should I enter each course or just my overall percentage?
questions.a: Enter each course if you can. US schools weigh every course by its credits, so a course-by-course GPA is closer to what an evaluator calculates. The overall percentage gives a quick estimate only.

questions.q: What is the difference between the 4.0 and 4.3 scales?
questions.a: Most US application forms use the 4.0 scale, where A+ and A are both worth 4.0. Some schools use 4.3, where A+ is worth 4.3. Use the scale the application form asks for.

questions.q: Is this GPA accepted by US universities?
questions.a: It is an unofficial estimate for application forms that ask you to self-report a GPA. Universities that require an official evaluation, such as WES, calculate their own GPA, which may differ.
